# Game model (color-sequence "nested list" puzzle)

## Layout
- Top strip: LEGEND = ordered list of N outlined color squares = the target sequence.
- Middle: one main box (red, white corner brackets) plus zero or more sub-boxes (green/blue/...).
  - Cells inside a box show a small GRAY DOT = fillable slot.
  - A cell drawn as a colored RING (no gray dot) is a POINTER to the sub-box of that same color;
    it is not fillable. A corridor of that color links it to its sub-box.
- Bottom strip: PALETTE of unplaced colored squares (each used exactly once).
- Total fillable slots == number of legend colors == number of palette pieces.

## Rule (confirmed L1-L3)
Flatten the structure by reading the main box left->right; when a pointer cell is reached,
recursively read that sub-box left->right, then continue in the parent box.
The flattened sequence of slot colors must equal the legend order.

## Controls
- ACTION6 on a palette piece: selects it (white halo).
- ACTION6 on a slot: places selected piece there (palette entry becomes a gray dot).
- ACTION5: submit/confirm when all slots filled -> advances level (progress +1).
- ACTION7: undo.
- No RESET needed; level advances automatically after ACTION5.

## Practical notes
- Read exact coordinates with read_pixels (legend row y~22, palette row y~472,
  box rows vary). Slot centers = gray dot centers.
- 8 levels total; complexity grows (more colors, more/nested sub-boxes).

[After action · write GUIDE.md]
# Game model: "nested list / pointer" color-sequence puzzle (8 levels) — SOLVED

## Screen layout
- Top strip: LEGEND = the target flattened sequence of colors (outlined squares, read left->right,
  and top row then bottom row if two rows).
- Middle: boxes. The box with WHITE CORNER BRACKETS is the ROOT list. Other colored boxes are sub-lists.
  - Cell with a small GRAY DOT = empty slot (fillable).
  - Cell drawn as a colored RING = POINTER to the sub-box of that same color (not fillable).
  - A colored box may have its own color pre-filled as its first cell (fixed, counts in the sequence).
- Bottom strip: PALETTE pieces, each usable exactly once: solid color squares and RING pieces
  (a ring piece placed in a slot becomes a pointer to the box of that color).
- Invariant: (#empty slots) == (#palette pieces).

## Rule
Flatten the root list left->right; on a pointer cell, recurse into that box (left->right), then continue.
The flattened color sequence must equal the legend. Cycles are allowed (level 8): pointers may form a
loop, producing an infinite periodic sequence; the legend then shows the period repeated (e.g. 2x6=12).

## Controls
- ACTION6 on palette piece = select (white halo); ACTION6 on a slot = place there.
- ACTION5 = submit once all slots are filled -> level advances automatically (no RESET needed).
- ACTION7 = undo. Minimum cost per level = 2 x (#slots) + 1.

## Method that worked
1. read_pixels on legend row (y~22), palette row (y~470), and each box's dot row (1-4 px bins)
   to get exact colors and center coordinates.
2. Decompose the legend into contiguous runs matching each sub-box (a sub-box's fixed first color
   pins where its run starts; run length = box size).
3. Place all pieces, then ACTION5. Placement order is irrelevant.

[After action · message]
Completed the game (8/8 levels, terminal state **WIN**).

**Model discovered and used:** each level is a "nested list" puzzle — the top strip is the target flattened color sequence, the white-bracketed box is the root list, colored rings are pointers that expand into the same-colored sub-box, and the palette supplies exactly as many pieces as empty slots. Solving = decomposing the legend into runs matching each sub-box, placing every piece (select piece → click slot), then `ACTION5` to submit.

Key escalations across levels: single list → one nested sub-list → two sub-lists → placeable pointer pieces → the same sub-list referenced twice → 3 sub-lists in a 2×2 layout → chained nesting (root→blue→green) → mutually recursive pointers forming a cycle whose period‑6 expansion matched the 12-square legend.
